meaning.collected: evidence the watches record by themselves (trades, shadows, sightings, looks)
meaning.forwarded: a question sent to the repair shop because the evidence pointed at a possible problem or opportunity
meaning.verdict: PASS = may change the live paper system; FAIL = nothing changes; the lesson is kept
meaning.in_use: a repair that passed and now runs in paper, tracked against its expectation

reviews.title: Explorer scorecard: entries, warning bells, weakest setup
reviews.forwarded_because: The 7-year Explorer replay lost money after costs. Three things looked suspicious: limit orders that never filled seemed to do better, the warning-bell exits seemed to cut winners, and setup E5 was the worst.
reviews.question: Do market entries, no warning bells, or dropping E5 make the Explorer better on data it was not tuned on?
reviews.result: No change passed. Market entries were clearly worse. The 'missed orders did better' evidence was hindsight bias (our error). Bells neither help nor hurt normally but save money in crashes, so they stay. E5 is the weakest setup but not by enough to drop.
reviews.changed: Nothing in the live rules. Scorecard wording corrected; the chase shadow no longer counts as evidence about entries.

reviews.title: Learning from other traders (Hyperliquid, 65 accounts)
reviews.forwarded_because: Our own setups showed no edge, so we checked where real traders entered and whether their timing carries information our rules miss.
reviews.question: Is there usable information in when real traders buy, and does their skill persist?
reviews.result: Their entry timing carried almost no information (a tiny 1-hour edge) and skill did not persist from one period to the next. One pattern stood out: they did better buying weakness than strength. That became review #3.
reviews.changed: Nothing live. Traders stay reference only, never teachers.

reviews.title: Buying weakness (dip setups E6-E8)
reviews.forwarded_because: Review #2 found traders did better buying dips.
reviews.question: Do dip entries beat random entries and pay NDAX costs on 2017-2023 data?
reviews.result: Buying when 15m RSI is under 30 beat random entries (first rule ever to beat chance on unseen data) but by far too little to pay fees and spread. Every variant lost after costs.
reviews.changed: Dip setups E6-E8 are watched only (sightings for the atlas), never traded.

reviews.title: Portfolio trend layer (T3) vs buy-and-hold
reviews.forwarded_because: Reviews #1-#3 showed the only consistent return is being in the market during multi-week uptrends, and the only consistent protection is getting out in slow crashes.
reviews.question: Can a simple daily trend rule (hold a coin above its 50- and 20-day averages while BTC is above its 50-day) beat buy-and-hold with less pain?
reviews.result: T3 passed: +13% vs buy-and-hold -22% in 2024-26 with about half the drawdown, and it sat out most crashes. Weak spot: it fails if fees double, so it must trade rarely.
reviews.changed: T3 runs as the portfolio layer (MAIN book you approve, SHADOW book always automatic) since 2026-09-30.

reviews.title: Madhav's reads: capitulation, higher-low retest, quiet base
reviews.forwarded_because: Madhav's four SOL buys (Jun-Aug 2026) gained +56% to +94% while Ananta's dip buys were shaken out; the casebook rebuild showed what he saw at each buy.
reviews.question: When the market shows what he saw at those buys, does buying beat buying a random day (2018-2023 tested, 2024-July 2026 confirm)?
reviews.result: The reader caught all four of his buys on the right days. On their own the reads did not beat a random day in 2018-2023 (2022 capitulations kept falling); since 2024 all did better, on few events.
reviews.changed: Nothing in the Explorer. The reads show live as 'Your setups' (Markets, coin pages, Ask Ananta) with their history; the phone rings only for a supported read.

reviews.title: Do zones hold?
reviews.forwarded_because: Madhav: it is always a zone; every study had used single price points.
reviews.question: Does price hold at zones more often than at random bands of the same width?
reviews.result: A little: the 200-day average, overlapping zones and new swing zones pass; a level that held twice was not stronger; entering a zone gives no return by itself.
reviews.changed: Zone map live on Markets and coin pages; zone entries recorded.

reviews.title: The lookout: reactions inside a zone
reviews.forwarded_because: Review #6: entering a zone is not a trade; what happens inside decides.
reviews.question: Which reactions at a support zone separate held from broken?
reviews.result: Only the market regime (BTC above its 50-day): 68% held vs 50%. Wicks, closes back above, volume, divergence, relative strength added nothing beyond arithmetic.
reviews.changed: Lookout and attention live; the playbook puts the market first.

reviews.title: Your setups with zones and the market gate
reviews.forwarded_because: Reviews #6-#7 found what matters at a support.
reviews.question: Do your setups work at supported zones and/or with the market allowed?
reviews.result: No pass. The higher-low retest with the market allowed is the most promising (12 episodes, 11 up after 30 days, +20%) but one event short of the bar; zones did not help.
reviews.changed: The retest with the market allowed is recorded live as its own read.

reviews.title: Explorer setups with zones
reviews.forwarded_because: The Explorer's support is recent 1-hour swings, not zones.
reviews.question: Do the Explorer's entries do better at zones or with the market allowed?
reviews.result: Zones did not help its hours-long trades; the market gate helped (-$0.17 vs -$0.66 per $100) but they still lose. Daily zones act over weeks.
reviews.changed: Nothing in the Explorer; zone work continues on the weeks-long books.

reviews.title: Stops and exits at zones
reviews.forwarded_because: Zones work over weeks; the exit decides what a zone entry earns.
reviews.question: Is a stop beyond the zone with a target at the next zone better than holding, an ATR stop or a tight stop?
reviews.result: No: the next zone is near, so the target sold the few big moves early (0% vs +5.8% holding 20 days). Gains come from a few big moves.
reviews.changed: The playbook treats the next zone as a review point, not a sell target.

reviews.title: Teacher ideas with zones: 50-day dip, breakouts
reviews.forwarded_because: Every earlier study used points; the teachers' pullback and breakout ideas had never been tested as zones.
reviews.question: Do a dip into the 50-day zone, or a close through a zone (strong resistance, volume), beat an average day in the same market?
reviews.result: No. The market regime does the work; the dip was worse than average; breakouts on volume were positive in both periods but not reliable.
reviews.changed: H11 marked not supported; H09 keeps its hypothesis status with these numbers.

reviews.title: T3's exit vs trailing stops
reviews.forwarded_because: Reviews #10-#11: gains come from a few big moves; would a looser exit keep more of them?
reviews.question: Do a zone trail, a 3-ATR chandelier or a 50-day exit beat T3's 20-day exit in both periods?
reviews.result: No. They tripled 2018-23 (trending) but lost 7-26% in 2024-26 (choppy) while T3 made +13%. T3's tight exit is the one that survives both.
reviews.changed: Nothing; T3 stays. A regime-aware exit is a new idea.

in_use.what: Portfolio trend layer: daily ratings, weekly rebalance, MAIN (you approve) and SHADOW (automatic) books
in_use.expect: Beat buy-and-hold over months mainly by losing less in slides; about half the drawdown; few trades
in_use.watch_out: Fails at double fees; one month proves nothing

safety_changes.what: Kill switch rehearsal passed: flattens every paper position and blocks new entries
Single-watch lock: a second copy of a watch refuses to start (we once ran two by accident)
Phone alerts (ntfy) for trades, warnings and errors
Nightly reconstruction: the day is rebuilt from raw candles and must match the live log
Jarvis app: Face ID before approve, mode change or kill switch; every action audited
Ask Ananta can only PREPARE changes (paper orders, alerts, mandate edits); each waits for your Face ID confirmation
Your manual paper orders live in their own book, never mixed with the agent's evidence
AI cost controls: Ask and Voice switches, daily Claude budget with free fallback

studies.title: Other traders' trades (Hyperliquid)
studies.runs: once (a study, not a daily job)
studies.their_timing_edge: +0.06% in the first hour (about a tenth of costs)
studies.what_we_did: Nothing copied. Their one pattern (buying weakness did better) was tested in review #3 on 2017-2023 data.

modes.what: Paper wide mode: E6 dips traded on paper; up to 3 trades per coin per type when at least 2 four-hour ranges apart; 60 entries a day
modes.why: More paper evidence per day (Q1 needed ~2 weeks at the old pace). Same $100 size, exits and warning bells.
modes.watch_out: Trades on the same coin at the same moment repeat one result: read 'independent events', not just the trade count.
